answers.core: UX improvement for existing core functionality.
answers.workaround:
UX improvement for signal rigging. Signal rigging happens a lot.

Let's ballpark for a decently-sized game with many of these connections (my case): 120 levels × 100 uses (not all are permanent, level design is iterative) = 12 000 uses. If the current workflow involves a minute of scrolling to find the right node with the right name in the dialogue window and this proposal cuts it down to a relatively negligible time, that's 12 000 minutes, or 200 hours of annoying gruntwork gone. Per that decently-sized game. Seems **often** enough for this type of game. Will improve UX for all other types of games, just not as dramatically, but still, in a meaningful way.

This could be worked around by creating your own editor inside the game. That's not a solution, that's a symptom of a lacking Godot editor functionality and another way to spend the 200 hours, (provided one has the skills to take that advanced path).

title: Ability to connect signals in the editor with drag-and-drop and name search
